title: Introduction to lwpls
text: query sample xqx_q, similarity weight training sample xix_i ωi=exp⁡(−diσdφ),di=‖xi−xq‖, \omega_i = \exp\left(-\frac{d_i}{\sigma_d \, \varphi}\right), \qquad d_i = \lVert x_i - x_q \rVert, σd\sigma_d standard deviation distances did_i φ>0\varphi > 0 localization parameter. training data centered weighted means, PLS model num_comp components fitted using weights ωi\omega_i, query projected onto local model get prediction. two main hyperparameters therefore: num_comp: number PLS components local models; localization: small values make models local (nearest samples matter); large values make weights similar, LW-PLS tends global PLS model. Optionally, neighbors restricts local model nearest training samples (“KNN-LW” strategy compared original LW-PLS Lesnoff et al., 2020).

what: Regression: fat-free water content of meat from NIR spectra
title: Introduction to lwpls
text: meats data modeldata package contain 100 near-infrared absorbance values 215 meat samples. predict water content. model specification marks hyperparameters tuning. Since LW-PLS calculates local models prediction time, values num_comp obtained model, tune fits one model per value localization (“submodel trick”).  local models (small localization) quickly -fit, large values reproduce global PLS. best models lie . finalize workflow best parameters evaluate test set:
code: data(meats, package = "modeldata") meats <- meats[, !names(meats) %in% c("fat", "protein")]  set.seed(123) meats_split <- initial_split(meats, prop = 0.75) meats_train <- training(meats_split) meats_test <- testing(meats_split) meats_folds <- vfold_cv(meats_train, v = 5) lwpls_spec <-   lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = tune()) |>   set_mode("regression")  lwpls_wflow <- workflow(water ~ ., lwpls_spec)  lwpls_grid <- dials::grid_regular(   dials::num_comp(c(1, 15)),   localization(),   levels = c(num_comp = 15, localization = 8) )  lwpls_res <- tune_grid(   lwpls_wflow,   resamples = meats_folds,   grid = lwpls_grid,   metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq) )  show_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse", n = 5) #> # A tibble: 5 × 8 #>   num_comp localization .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config           #>      <int>        <dbl> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>             #> 1       10          0.5 rmse    standard    1.66     5   0.156 pre0_mod077_post0 #> 2       13          0.5 rmse    standard    1.68     5   0.198 pre0_mod101_post0 #> 3        9          0.5 rmse    standard    1.70     5   0.174 pre0_mod069_post0 #> 4        8          0.5 rmse    standard    1.71     5   0.184 pre0_mod061_post0 #> 5       12          0.5 rmse    standard    1.77     5   0.194 pre0_mod093_post0 autoplot(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse") +   scale_color_viridis_d(option = "mako", end = 0.9) +   theme_bw() best_params <- select_best(lwpls_res, metric = "rmse") best_params #> # A tibble: 1 × 3 #>   num_comp localization .config           #>      <int>        <dbl> <chr>             #> 1       10          0.5 pre0_mod077_post0  lwpls_final <-   lwpls_wflow |>   finalize_workflow(best_params) |>   last_fit(meats_split)  collect_metrics(lwpls_final) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       1.38  pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.978 pre0_mod0_post0

code: pls_wflow <- workflow(   water ~ .,   lwpls(num_comp = tune(), localization = 1e6) |> set_mode("regression") ) pls_res <- tune_grid(   pls_wflow,   resamples = meats_folds,   grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:15),   metrics = metric_set(rmse, rsq) )  pls_final <-   pls_wflow |>   finalize_workflow(select_best(pls_res, metric = "rmse")) |>   last_fit(meats_split)  collect_metrics(pls_final) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>   .metric .estimator .estimate .config         #>   <chr>   <chr>          <dbl> <chr>           #> 1 rmse    standard       2.40  pre0_mod0_post0 #> 2 rsq     standard       0.933 pre0_mod0_post0 test_preds <- rbind(   data.frame(model = "Global PLS", collect_predictions(pls_final)),   data.frame(model = "LW-PLS", collect_predictions(lwpls_final)) )  ggplot(test_preds, aes(water, .pred)) +   geom_abline(color = "grey50", linetype = 2) +   geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +   facet_wrap(~model) +   coord_obs_pred() +   labs(x = "Observed water (%)", y = "Predicted water (%)") +   theme_bw()

title: Introduction to lwpls
text: factor outcome, LW-PLS models class indicators: locally weighted partial least squares-discriminant analysis (LW-PLS-DA, Bevilacqua Marini, 2014). predicted class one largest predicted indicator, indicators, truncated [0,1][0, 1], give class probabilities. every local model linear fitted around query, LW-PLS-DA can follow curved class boundaries global PLS-DA model . parabolic data modeldata illustrate : two classes separated parabola plane predictors X1 X2. two predictors, local models two components, tune localization :  Performance drops steadily models become global. compare tuned LW-PLS-DA model global PLS-DA (large localization) test set: decision regions show . global model can separate classes straight line, local models bend boundary along parabola. shading predicted probability Class1, black line 0.5 contour, points test samples:  ROC curves test set summarize difference across probability thresholds:  Finally, confusion matrix LW-PLS-DA model test set:  Note regions without training data, upper-left corner, local models extrapolate nearest samples, predictions -interpreted. two classes, model works way returns one .pred_{level} probability column per class.
code: data(parabolic, package = "modeldata")  set.seed(91) para_split <- initial_split(parabolic, strata = class) para_train <- training(para_split) para_test <- testing(para_split) para_folds <- vfold_cv(para_train, v = 5, strata = class) lwplsda_wflow <- workflow(   class ~ .,   lwpls(num_comp = 2, localization = tune()) |> set_mode("classification") )  lwplsda_res <- tune_grid(   lwplsda_wflow,   resamples = para_folds,   grid = data.frame(localization = 2^seq(-6, 5)),   metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy) )  show_best(lwplsda_res, metric = "roc_auc", n = 3) #> # A tibble: 3 × 7 #>   localization .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err .config          #>          <dbl> <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl> <chr>            #> 1       0.25   roc_auc binary     0.962     5 0.00424 pre0_mod05_post0 #> 2       0.125  roc_auc binary     0.961     5 0.00488 pre0_mod04_post0 #> 3       0.0625 roc_auc binary     0.959     5 0.00337 pre0_mod03_post0 autoplot(lwplsda_res) +   theme_bw() lwplsda_final <-   lwplsda_wflow |>   finalize_workflow(select_best(lwplsda_res, metric = "roc_auc")) |>   last_fit(para_split, metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy))  plsda_final <-   workflow(     class ~ .,     lwpls(num_comp = 2, localization = 1e6) |> set_mode("classification")   ) |>   last_fit(para_split, metrics = metric_set(roc_auc, accuracy))  rbind(   data.frame(model = "LW-PLS-DA", collect_metrics(lwplsda_final)),   data.frame(model = "Global PLS-DA", collect_metrics(plsda_final)) )[, c("model", ".metric", ".estimate")] #>           model  .metric .estimate #> 1     LW-PLS-DA accuracy 0.9200000 #> 2     LW-PLS-DA  roc_auc 0.9728484 #> 3 Global PLS-DA accuracy 0.6640000 #> 4 Global PLS-DA  roc_auc 0.7612705 para_grid <- expand.grid(   X1 = seq(min(parabolic$X1), max(parabolic$X1), length.out = 100),   X2 = seq(min(parabolic$X2), max(parabolic$X2), length.out = 100) )  region_probs <- function(final, model) {   probs <- predict(extract_workflow(final), para_grid, type = "prob")   data.frame(para_grid, model = model, .pred_Class1 = probs$.pred_Class1) }  regions <- rbind(   region_probs(plsda_final, "Global PLS-DA"),   region_probs(lwplsda_final, "LW-PLS-DA") )  ggplot(regions, aes(X1, X2)) +   geom_raster(aes(fill = .pred_Class1), alpha = 0.8) +   geom_contour(aes(z = .pred_Class1), breaks = 0.5, color = "black") +   geom_point(data = para_test, aes(shape = class), color = "white", size = 2.6) +   geom_point(data = para_test, aes(shape = class, color = class), size = 1.6) +   facet_wrap(~model) +   scale_fill_distiller(palette = "RdBu", direction = 1, limits = c(0, 1)) +   scale_color_manual(values = c(Class1 = "#08306B", Class2 = "#67000D")) +   coord_equal(expand = FALSE) +   labs(fill = "Probability\nof Class1", color = NULL, shape = NULL) +   theme_bw() test_roc <- function(final, model) {   roc <- roc_curve(collect_predictions(final), truth = class, .pred_Class1)   data.frame(model = model, roc) }  roc_data <- rbind(   test_roc(lwplsda_final, "LW-PLS-DA"),   test_roc(plsda_final, "Global PLS-DA") )  ggplot(roc_data, aes(1 - specificity, sensitivity, color = model)) +   geom_abline(color = "grey50", linetype = 2) +   geom_path(linewidth = 0.8) +   scale_color_manual(values = c("LW-PLS-DA" = "#08519C", "Global PLS-DA" = "#969696")) +   coord_equal() +   labs(color = NULL) +   theme_bw() collect_predictions(lwplsda_final) |>   conf_mat(truth = class, estimate = .pred_class) |>   autoplot(type = "heatmap")

title: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for tidymodels
text: lwpls implements locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) tidymodels ecosystem. LW-PLS just--time learning method used chemometrics process monitoring (soft sensors). Instead fitting single global model, builds dedicated weighted PLS model around new sample, every training sample weighted similarity sample. linear method can therefore capture nonlinear time-varying relationships.

title: Locally-Weighted Partial Least Squares for tidymodels
text: lwpls(): parsnip model regression (one outcomes) classification (LW-PLS-DA). native implementation, validated Kaneko’s reference implementation, prediction kernel written C++ (RcppArmadillo). Queries processed blocks, work runs BLAS matrix-matrix products. Tuning tune dials: localization() tuning parameter, values num_comp evaluated single fit (“submodel trick”). lwpls_fit(): standalone hardhat modeling function matrix, data frame, formula recipe interfaces.

title: Locally-weighted partial least squares — lwpls
text: lwpls() defines locally-weighted partial least squares (LW-PLS) model use parsnip package. LW-PLS just--time (lazy) learner: instead fitting one global model, dedicated weighted PLS model built around every new sample, training sample weighted similarity sample. lets linear method capture nonlinear time-varying relationships, makes popular soft sensors spectroscopic calibration. model can used regression (one numeric outcomes) classification (discriminant analysis class indicators). single engine, "lwpls", implemented package (C++ via RcppArmadillo).

title: Locally-weighted partial least squares — lwpls
text: mode single character string prediction outcome mode. Possible values "unknown", "regression", "classification". num_comp number PLS components (latent variables) local model (engine default: 2). localization positive number controlling local models (engine default: 1). Small values give large weights closest training samples ; large values give samples similar weights, LW-PLS tends global PLS model. See Details. neighbors number nearest training samples used local model. default (NULL) uses training samples, original LW-PLS algorithm. engine single character string specifying computational engine. "lwpls" available.

title: Locally-weighted partial least squares — lwpls
text: query sample \(x_q\), similarity weight training sample \(x_i\) $$\omega_i = \exp\left(-\frac{d_i}{\sigma_d \, \varphi}\right),$$ \(d_i = \lVert x_i - x_q \rVert\) Euclidean distance (standardized predictors default), \(\sigma_d\) standard deviation distances \(\varphi\) localization parameter (\(\lambda\) Kaneko's implementation). weighted PLS model fitted weighted centering, weighted covariances query projected onto local latent space obtain prediction. neighbors set, neighbors closest training samples receive non-zero weight \(\sigma_d\) computed distances. "KNN-LW" strategy, Lesnoff et al. (2020) compare original LW-PLS weights training samples. classification, outcome converted class indicator columns modeled multi-response LW-PLS (LW-PLS-DA; Bevilacqua Marini, 2014). predicted class one largest predicted indicator. Class probabilities obtained truncating predicted indicators [0, 1] renormalizing sum one. LW-PLS lazy learner, fitting stores (standardized) training data; computational work happens prediction time. prediction num_comp components also yields predictions smaller numbers components, tune::tune_grid() evaluates every value num_comp single model ("submodel trick").

code: train <- mtcars[-(1:5), ] test <- mtcars[1:5, ]  # XY interface fit <- lwpls_fit(train[, -1], train$mpg, num_comp = 3, localization = 0.5) fit #> Locally-weighted PLS (regression) #>  #> Training samples: 27  #> Predictors:       10 (standardized)  #> Components:       3  #> Localization:     0.5  #> Neighbors:        all (27)  predict(fit, test[, -1]) #> # A tibble: 5 × 1 #>   .pred #>   <dbl> #> 1  21.1 #> 2  20.7 #> 3  27.0 #> 4  18.8 #> 5  17.4  # Formula interface, with two outcomes fit2 <- lwpls_fit(mpg + qsec ~ ., data = train, num_comp = 3) predict(fit2, test) #> # A tibble: 5 × 2 #>   .pred_mpg .pred_qsec #>       <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1      22.1       16.4 #> 2      21.7       16.4 #> 3      28.6       18.9 #> 4      19.2       20.0 #> 5      16.8       16.9  # Classification fit3 <- lwpls_fit(Species ~ ., data = iris, num_comp = 2) predict(fit3, iris[c(1, 51, 101), ], type = "prob") #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   .pred_setosa .pred_versicolor .pred_virginica #>          <dbl>            <dbl>           <dbl> #> 1      0.990            0.00970           0     #> 2      0.0269           0.502             0.471 #> 3      0.00553          0.0235            0.971

title: lwpls 0.2.0
text: lwpls() now arguments mode, num_comp, localization, neighbors engine. shapefactor argument replaced localization, parameter similarity function Kim et al. (2011) (lambda Kaneko’s implementation). engine now "lwpls" ("rnirs"). magrittr pipe %>% generics::tidy() longer re-exported. Use native pipe |> (R >= 4.1.0).

title: lwpls 0.2.0
text: Native implementation LW-PLS, validated Kaneko’s reference implementation. prediction kernel written C++ (RcppArmadillo): uses kernel PLS algorithm Dayal & MacGregor (1997) processes queries blocks work runs BLAS matrix-matrix products. Regression one numeric outcomes, classification (LW-PLS-DA) class probability predictions. New lwpls_fit(), hardhat-based fitting function matrix, data frame, formula recipe interfaces. predict() method returns tibbles follow tidymodels conventions can use number components. multi_predict() min_grid() methods: tune evaluates values num_comp single model fit. New dials tuning parameter localization(). optional neighbors argument restricts local model nearest training samples. "lwpls" engine scale argument switch standardization data. Added unit tests (test coverage tracked Codecov) introductory vignette (vignette("lwpls")), including regression classification examples.
